question: Does sizing by a volatility forecast change the volatility and drawdown of a fixed always-long basket?
edge_claim: none. Report-only: it decides nothing, adds no feature, and reopens no closed line
period: development test folds 2013-2022 only; nothing after 2022-12-31 is loaded
basket: every U1 stock trade at h = 1 on each signal date from the frozen development rows: long, entry at the open after the signal, exit at that close. Equal weight across names each date

sizers.har: weight = min(2, 0.30 / HAR forecast annualised x sqrt(252)). HAR: least squares of log forward volatility on log rv_5, log rv_20, log rv_60, fitted on rows before each fold less a purge of 1 session, as spec c

same_rows: only trades where all three sizers have a value, so every sizer has identical names and dates
inputs_known_at: features for signal D read D-1, as features_v1
metrics: annualised volatility of the daily basket return
maximum drawdown of the running sum of daily returns, in percent of notional
mean absolute day-to-day change in weight per name
scaled_view: each sizer also rescaled to the constant sizer's realised volatility, labelled hindsight scaling, so that drawdown can be compared on equal risk
costs: gross, and net at 1.5x costs times the weight; cost model unverified
reading_rule: lower volatility or drawdown says only that sizing changed risk over this period. Lower risk is not an edge. Any use needs its own decision
